source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix Json<UpdateOperations> extractor (update_api.rs:331) -> serde deserializes Vec<UpdateOperation> -> UpdateOperation is #[serde(untagged)] (update.rs:99) so serde tries variants in DECLARATION order -> Upsert(UpsertOperation) is first (update.rs:101); UpsertOperation (update.rs:255-259) has the single field `upsert` and no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], so the extra `delete` key is silently ignored -> UpdateOperation::Upsert accepted -> no key-count/ambiguity validation exists anywhere downstream (the Validate impl at update.rs:111-124 only delegates to the inner-op validators; the handler passes operations straight to do_batch_update_points at update_api.rs:349). This mechanism also explains live probe P2: JSON key order is irrelevant because the winner is fixed by enum declaration order, and it explains why zero-key (F5), unknown-key (F6) and nested-type-violation forms (domain_006 N1-N5) are rejected with 'data did not match any variant of untagged enum UpdateOperation' while the two-known-keys form is not.
